messages:
incident-bot: PAGE — streaming p99 tail latency breached for /v1/generate-stream in eu-west-1 (threshold 3s). alert: p99=5.7s, p95=0.8s. Paging on-call.

pagerduty-bot: @sam you're on-call — PD INC-8241. Please acknowledge.

Sam: acked. I'm taking the page. starting root-cause checklist.

Marta (SRE): quick summary from dashboards: p95 ~ 800ms, p99 ~ 5.7s. Streaming stalls correlating with KV cache miss spikes and per-node queue depth increases. Looks localized to a single GPU node group.

Devin (eng-runtime): pulling logs — seeing repeated ECC correctable increments and fan PWM oscillation on gpu-57. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:21:12Z] nvml: ecc_corrected_count ++ (gpu-57)
[2026-03-15T09:21:13Z] nvml: fan_pwm 25 -> 85 -> 25 (oscillation)
[2026-03-15T09:21:13Z] runtime: GPU_THROTTLE thermal_limit engaged
[2026-03-15T09:21:13Z] streaming: stall detected, kv_cache_miss_ratio 0.38 -> 0.75
```
This pattern repeats ~every 8s.

Sam: that would explain power capping -> compute throughput drop -> KV eviction thrash -> tail lat spikes.

Kai (infra): I'm starting an immediate drain of gpu-57. running: 
```
redwoodctl nodes drain gpu-57 --evacuate-streams --reason "fan-oscillation-thermal-throttle"
```
ETA for node to finish eviction ~2m. Will also mark for quarantine.

Marta (SRE): while drain proceeds, enable fallback routing for the streaming endpoint to the fallback model variant to avoid more customer session failures. reduce streaming concurrency.

Devin (eng-runtime): toggled runtime flags: reroute ~22% traffic -> fallback-model-streaming (eu-west-1), set streaming_concurrency=1 for fallback, enabled aggressive KV prefix caching for in-flight requests.

incident-bot: Fallback routing applied. Traffic shifted ~22% to fallback-model-streaming. Autoscaling notice sent.

Sam: observing metrics — p99 dropped from 5.7s -> ~1.9s within 2m of reroute. p95 stable ~600ms. Good short-term.

Marta (SRE): customer-impact: two reserved-capacity customers in eu-west-1 reported degraded sessions; one session aborted. CS ticket creation initiated. Please prepare outreach.

Kai (infra): digging hardware telemetry — fan PWM toggling 30% <-> 90% every ~8s, thermal excursions observed but not sustained over thresholds; ECC correctable errors rising. Creating colo hardware ticket TICKET-7745 for fan controller / GPU board swap.

Devin (eng-runtime): also seeing driver backoffs and repeated device resets in dmesg on gpu-57. marking node as flaky and adding to quarantine list.

Sam: PD incident updated and being closed from active paging, but I'll keep monitoring for 1hr. setting reminder to re-check p99 in 15/30/60m.

Marta (SRE): immediate mitigation notes: 1) evacuated node gpu-57 2) traffic reroute to fallback model 3) reduced concurrency 4) increased KV prefix caching — these together reduced tail impact.

Devin (eng-runtime): commands used: 
```
# drain
redwoodctl nodes drain gpu-57 --evacuate-streams --grace 120
# reroute
redwoodctl traffic set-route /v1/generate-stream --fallback-model fallback-model-streaming --percent 22
# lower concurrency
redwoodctl runtime update-policy streaming --concurrency 1
```

Kai (infra): colo ticket TICKET-7745 created. ETA hardware swap 6h, on-site engineer assigned. Requesting temp warm spare allocation in eu-west-1 to reduce single-node blast radius.

Marta (SRE): post-incident action items (ACTIONS):
- A1 (devin): add runtime auto-evacuate trigger for fan PWM oscillation & repeated ECC correctables.
- A2 (kai): hardware swap gpu-57, run ECC stress test, confirm stability.
- A3 (sam): customer comms & CS handoff for affected accounts.
- A4 (marta): draft postmortem and add synthetic canary for streaming p99 and KV miss ratio.

Devin (eng-runtime): filed PR stub for auto-evacuate detection -> link placeholder https://redwood.internal/pulls/EVAC-2026 and incident postmortem stub https://redwood.internal/incidents/1739999999 (will flesh out).

Sam: leaving monitoring for 1h. if p99 < 2s for 30m we'll resolve.

Marta (SRE): one more recommendation — add an alert that fires on oscillating fan_pwm values (high variance) in addition to thermal threshold to catch controllers that oscillate frequently.

Kai (infra): agreed. adding alert -> colo ops + hardware diagnostics integration.

Devin (eng-runtime): note for follow-up: consider increasing warm spare pool in region or capacity buffer to avoid single node causing >20% traffic fallback.

ops-bot: PD INC-8241 status -> acknowledged -> mitigated -> monitoring.

Sam: thanks team. I'll update the PD, CS, and close active page once stable for 30m. :thumbsup:
